$comment: The model registry and routing policy. Models are data: add or adjust one in your own ~/.claude/model-router.json, or per project in .claude/model-router.json (same shape, merged key by key). strength and cost are relative ranks. A model's name must be an alias the Agent tool accepts (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable). Levels pair a strength with an effort: a level runs on the cheapest model at or above its strength, so standard runs on Sonnet at medium, complex on Opus at high, and hardest differs from complex in effort on the same model: Opus at xhigh. A model named on a call stands for its lowest level, and gets that level's effort when nobody chose one. A model weaker than a level needs runs it one effort step higher, up to xhigh. No effort the router sets, a redo's included, goes past a model's effort_stops_at, except the session's own level on the session's own model. Prices are USD per million tokens on the Anthropic API, read only by the benchmark's cost estimate: Model Router prices nothing, and /model-router:usage shows Claude Code's own estimate. A key is one model version, or ends in -* to cover every version of a family. cache_write is the five-minute cache write price and cache_write_1h the one-hour one. `schema` is the version of this shape; an override may carry it too, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Compatibility" says what changes it.

haiku.use_for: Lookups, file search, summarizing known code, running a command and reporting, formatting, trivial edits.

sonnet.use_for: Everyday implementation at medium effort: features with a clear spec, tests, refactors inside one module.

opus.use_for: Defect fixes, migrations and performance work, design and planning, cross-module changes, subtle bugs, security-sensitive code, adversarial review.

fable.use_for: Research-grade and open-ended work: ambiguous multi-system problems with no known approach, long investigations, and retries after Opus fell short.

newest.$comment: The newest full model ID of each family that some provider's alias lags behind. Every provider in older_aliases takes this Claude API form: Bedrock and Agent Platform map it to their own ID, Foundry sends it as the deployment name, and Claude Platform on AWS and Claude Models on Google Cloud use it as is (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview.md).

older_aliases.$comment: Per provider, each family whose alias resolves to an older model than newest names, and the ID of that model (the alias table in https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config.md). The mod sends the newest ID for these instead of the alias.
